cards.explanation: The answer is the tombs. Jesus gets out of the boat and is met by a man who is coming from the tombs. Verse 3 adds that this man had been living there. I think this part of his story is a heavy one, friends.

The answer is False. People bound him again and again, but Mark says he "…had broken the chains and shattered the shackles." Nothing they had could hold him. Keep that picture in your head, friends, because it makes the next moment hit even harder.

The word is strength. Mark says, "Now there was no one with the strength to subdue him." People had tried with chains and shackles, and none of it held. The chains were broken and the shackles shattered.

The answer is False. Mark says, "Night and day in the tombs and in the mountains he kept crying out and cutting himself with stones." It didn't stop when the sun came up. I think this is one of the heavy parts of the story, friends, and it's good to slow down for it.

The answer is that he runs and falls on his knees before Jesus. When he saw Jesus from a distance, "…he ran and fell on his knees before Him." This is the man nobody could hold, and he ends up kneeling. Jesus had already told the spirit to come out of him.

The answer is Son of the Most High God. The man shouts, "What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God?" Out of everyone on that shore, he says it out loud. He knows exactly who just got out of that boat.

The answer is True. The man shouts, "I beg You before God not to torture me!" It's a strange thing to hear from a man who just ran up to Jesus, friends. The next verse explains where it's coming from.

The answer is that Jesus told the spirit to come out of the man. Mark says Jesus had already declared, "Come out of this man, you unclean spirit!" That's Jesus speaking, and He speaks to the spirit directly. Everything the man shouts comes after that.
The name is Legion. Jesus asks, and the answer is, "My name is Legion…" Short answer, friends, but it says a lot. The rest of that verse tells us why that name fits.
The word is many. He says, “for we are many.” That's the reason for the name Legion. The name is all about how many they are.
The word is region. Mark says he begged Jesus repeatedly not to send them out of that region. They kept asking over and over.

The answer is that they ask to be sent to the pigs. The demons beg Jesus, "Send us to the pigs, so that we may enter them." They had begged not to be sent out of that region, and now they point to the herd on the hillside.
The answer is False. Mark says, "He gave them permission, and the unclean spirits came out and went into the pigs…" Jesus doesn't refuse. The unclean spirits come out of the man and go into the herd.

The answer is down the steep bank into the sea. The herd "…rushed down the steep bank into the sea and drowned in the water." That happened right after the unclean spirits came out and went into the pigs. Jesus had given them permission.
The word is thousand. Mark says the herd was "…about two thousand…" That's one very big herd, friends. All of it rushed down the steep bank into the sea.

The answer is sitting there, clothed and in his right mind. The people "…saw the man who had been possessed by the legion of demons sitting there, clothed and in his right mind…" That's a very different picture, friends, and Mark says it plainly.

The answer is True. Mark says they saw him "…sitting there, clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid." It's a short line, and the text doesn't tell us anything more about why. I think that was a lot to take in.

The answer is that they beg Jesus to leave their region. Mark says, "…the people began to beg Jesus to leave their region." This comes after those who had seen it described what happened to the man and the pigs. The text doesn't say why they ask.

The answer is that he begs to go with Jesus. As Jesus is getting into the boat, the man "…begged to go with Him." He wants to be right there with Jesus. Mark doesn't give a reason, but I'd say that's easy to understand.
The answer is False. Mark says, "But Jesus would not allow him." Instead Jesus says, “Go home to your own people…” The man doesn't get in the boat.

The words are Lord and mercy. Jesus says, “…how much the Lord has done for you, and what mercy He has shown you.” The man is told to share what the Lord has done, friends. He is sent to tell his own people about that mercy.

The answer is throughout the Decapolis. Mark says the man "…began to proclaim throughout the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him." The Decapolis is the region he goes through. And everyone was amazed.
